steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain.
In a large skillet, brown beef over medium heat. Add onions; saute until tender. Drain off fat and add spaghetti sauce; simmer for about 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

In a lightly greased 2 quart baking dish, place about half of the pasta; top with a layer of provolone and mozzarella cheese slices. Spread on a layer of half the spaghetti sauce mixture and sour cream.
Cover with remaining pasta, cheese and sauce; sprinkle a layer of Parmesan cheese and fresh basil.
Bake in preheated oven for about 30 minutes or until cheese and sauce are bubbly; serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Ziti III
raw_recipe.description: Layers of ziti pasta, beefy tomato sauce, sour cream and Italian cheeses get a final dash of flavor with a generous sprinkling of chopped fresh basil before baking.

review.reviewBody: Great recipe. I took the advice of another and tossed the ziti with the sour cream before layering. I will NEVER skip this step. The noodles stayed creamy and delicious. I browned ground pork, used left over ground beef, garlic and onion. I didn't have provolone so topped every layer with parmesan. I didn't need 2 jars of sauce as others said they did. very good.
No way this fits into a 2 qt casserole. Use you 9 x 13. I added 3 cloves chopped garlic with onion. Delish.

I give the flavor of this dish 5 stars but the recipe is written with way too much interpretation. It never tells you how to marry the sauce and sour cream and a few other things. With that being said, I used 1 1/2 cans of sauce to simmer and the other half I put a big scoop of sour cream in the remaining amount and mixed. I spread that over first layer. I put the rest of the sour cream and sauce in skillet with the onions and let that simmer. I doubled the meat and the cheese because we wanted meaty and cheesy and we got just that. The flavor that the sour cream brought to the dish was so good.

My whole family loves this, even picky grandchildren, which is saying something! To avoid the raw onion issue, I cooked them in a smidge of olive oil until translucent, then added the hamburger. Once the whole pot is simmering, I added @ 1 cup real shredded bacon bits, the kind you can find premade in the store. It added a smoky taste that enhanced the sauce. I also mixed the sour cream with the cooked pasta. Followed the recipe exactly with these minor tweaks. It makes a huge batch, so if I’m bringing a meal to someone, there’s enough to make a small casserole for the 2 of us. Using provolone cheese is a must IMO.Thank you for a wonderful recipe!

Winner! Have made this recipe so many times.....I first discovered it when a friend made it for Grandparent's day to serve to all of the visiting grandparents in the elementary school. I have since used it to feed guests at funeral luncheons, an anniversary party and countless meal deliveries to those in need of a meal. I was told to mix the sour cream into the pasta before layering, and I have never veered from that piece of advice. It is creamy and cheesy. My personal preference for sauce is Prego Traditional. Enjoy!

I substituted sweet Italian sausage for half of the ground beef, added 3 cloves of garlic, mixed the cooked ziti with 1 cup of the sour cream and used the remaining half cup of sour cream to spread between the layers of ziti. Thank you for the base recipe. Excellent dish. This is definitely a keeper.

YUM - YUM - YUMMMM! I made this the other night, with italian sausage instead of ground beef. I also took the advice of another reviewer & mixed the sour cream into the cooked noodles before layering (GREAT TIP!), used my 3.7 QT 9x13 glass baking dish...filled it perfectly! Hubby LOVED it as did I! DEFINITELY keeping this recipe in my dinner loop - thanks for posting it!

A KEEPER!
A delicious meal. I didnt use provolone cheese because I didnt have any. I used mozzarella and parmesan in the dish and on top. I also used whole wheat pasta. I didnt think I would like the whole wheat pasta in this dish because of the texture but took a chance anyway. I couldnt tell the difference so I'll keep this substitution. I used a 11×14 dish and both jars of spahaghetti sauce. I know many people said its too much but my family love cheese and I knew it would be on the drier side without extra sauce. It was prefect! So if you use the amount of cheese listed in this recipe, you will not need 2 jars but I used 6 oz shredded parmesan and nearly 4 cups shredded mozzarella Also, the suggestion to add the sour cream to the pasta first is genius- it makes the dish nice and creamy! I topped with dry basil- didnt have fresh. Even with the larger 11x14 dish on 350, it was still done in 30 minutes. Next time I will make sure I have provolone. I think it will be more delicious but even without it, it's a 5 star recipe.
Used 1 jar prego meat flavored and 1 jar basil, garlic flavored sauce! Froze and baked after complete thaw days later. Best ziti ever!
All 3 of us loved it, including my toddler! I took the notes about mixing the sour cream with the noodles and added oregano and garlic and will definitely be making it again!

This was so good! I made some tweaks based on other reviewers recommendations. I used mild Italian sausage rather than ground beef. I added a good amount of minced garlic and Italian seasoning to the sausage. I also mixed in the sour cream with the cooked noodles. This kept the noodles from drying out. I’ll be making this again!
I doubled the meat and added ricotta cheese and it's a keeper!

I’ve been using this exact recipe for nearly 20 years (it was last updated in 2022 but this definitely was on this site before 2006) and it’s always a hit. I’ve never mixed the sour cream with the pasta so I’m actually going to give that a try based off suggestions but always put a ladle of sauce on the bottom then make your layers because it helps pasta not stick or too dry when baked.
I have been making this recipe for years and it always gets completely eaten up! Great recipe.
Absolutely loved it! Guests thought it was awesome.
